title: Yaphank / Yamphanke
summary: Yaphank is a Brookhaven village name originally applied to a creek south of the hamlet. Yamphanke is an earlier recorded form.
history_content: The name is connected with a 1664 deed involving Unkechaug sachem Tobacus and a river called Yamphanke. The modern map point uses Yaphank and the Weeks Pond area as an approximate anchor.
translation_content:
The name has been translated as "the bank of a river." The exact source page is not yet strong enough to treat that translation as settled.

Why Place Names Matter

“Although the sachems repeatedly referred to Long Island as “Sewanhacky,” the mapmakers apparently paid attention only to the “mother maps,” which continued to be used as references for new maps. The name “Matouack” appears on three subsequent Dutch maps and on two English maps as late as 1755 and 1779.”

— John A. Strong, The Thirteen Tribes of Long Island: The History of a Myth (1992), Hudson Valley Regional Review, p. 50
preservation_content: Modern Yaphank is connected with an older creek and deed name while avoiding an exact claim about the historic river course.
whereintheworld_content: Approximate blue/general placement at Yaphank near Weeks Pond in Brookhaven town. Coordinates are approximate and not exact deed or creek boundaries.
